episodes.169593: Another active monsoon day impacted northern New Mexico on July 8, 2022, as thunderstorms developed across the mountainous terrain by early afternoon and becoming more widespread through the evening. Strong thunderstorms with heavy rainfall on the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar caused Tecolote Creek to exceed its banks, flooding area roadways. Meanwhile, a thunderstorm near Raton interacted with a boundary to briefly produce quarter size hail.
episodes.169603: Thunderstorms developed along the higher terrain to the north and moved towards the area. As storms moved into a highly unstable environment, they became more widespread and produced damaging winds, small hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.169610: During the morning hours of July 8th, thunderstorms remained nearly stationary across portions of central Indiana with a period of extremely heavy rain across much of Greene county and portions of Sullivan and Vigo counties. A quasi-tropical pattern led to increased rainfall rates with reports as great as 6.19 at the Graysville 5 WNW COOP site.
episodes.169744: Very hot temperatures on the afternoon of the eighth allowed for isolated thunderstorms to develop on the South Plains. Thunderstorms initially developed on an outflow boundary draped across the extreme southern Texas Panhandle that developed from early morning thunderstorms in the Texas Panhandle. A relatively dry sub-cloud layer enhanced the downburst potential of these storms. A few of these storms were able to produce severe wind gusts.
episodes.169817: Diurnal heating led to scattered thunderstorms, a couple of which produced wind damage.
episodes.169828: Isolated afternoon thunderstorms produced localized wind damage to mainly trees.
episodes.170053: Disturbances moved through a persistent southwest flow aloft across the region, which continued to provide daily afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms. These storms, some of which were severe, brought strong, gusty winds, severe hail, heavy localized rainfall, and lightning.
episodes.170414: Thunderstorms developed over the South Laramie Range foothills early in the afternoon on the 8th with a left-moving supercell moving across Goshen County producing golf ball sized hail near Torrington. Numerous storm reports noted the soft nature of the hailstones with some shattering upon impact.
episodes.170585: A surface low for a few days July 7th and 8th. While the parameter space was not conducive to strong convection, the steep lapse rates, low LCLs, and sufficient 0-3 km CAPE resulted in a favorable environment for funnel cloud development both days. Several funnel clouds were reported across central and northern Iowa, along with two tornadoes documented under developing storms during the afternoon of July 7th.  These spin-ups remained in open areas with little damage. Storms were also efficient rain producers, with a pocket of 3 to 5 inches in Hardin and Grundy counties.
episodes.170703: Scattered intense thunderstorms fired up during the heat of the day across southern Illinois. This activity developed ahead of a weak cold front and in the vicinity of a weak surface low centered over the mid Mississippi Valley. The atmosphere was quite unstable, with mixed-layer capes from 1500 to 2500 J/kg. Wind shear was sufficiently strong for isolated storms to become severe, with damaging wind gusts. Effective bulk shear was around 30 to 35 knots.
episodes.170705: Scattered intense thunderstorms fired up during the heat of the day across western Kentucky. This activity developed ahead of a weak cold front and in the vicinity of a weak surface low centered over the mid Mississippi Valley. The atmosphere was quite unstable, with mixed-layer capes from 1500 to 2500 J/kg. Wind shear was sufficiently strong for isolated storms to become severe, with damaging wind gusts. Effective bulk shear was around 30 to 35 knots. The storms maintained intensity through the evening and early night-time hours. Weak steering winds aloft contributed to slow storm movement and an isolated flash flood.
episodes.170986: An severe thunderstorm produced hail up to ping pong ball size southeast of Akron.
episodes.171047: A weak disturbance pressed into the Ohio Valley on July 8th, tapping into warm and muggy conditions permeating over West Virginia. This combination led to diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms that inflicted damaging wind gusts and heavy downpours in areas along the I-64 corridor. Multiple areas of downed trees and power lines were observed, as well as high water issues from Putnam County and eastward into the city of Charleston.
episodes.171184: Showers and thunderstorms passed through Lawrence County during the early afternoon of July 8th due to antecedent hot and muggy conditions. The strongest storms led to tree damage within the county.
episodes.171263: A thunderstorm became severe as it tracked south across western Meade County, weakening as it reached the Black Hills. The storm produced large hail east of Sturgis.
episodes.171479: A thunderstorm became severe for a brief time across the central Black Hills, producing large hail in the Hill City area.
episodes.171480: A severe thunderstorm over the northern Black Hills produced large hail in the Brownsville area.
episodes.171507: Multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms moved across Kentucky between July 6th and July 8th. The main focus for convection was areas along and just south of a quasi-stationary surface front, initially positioned from west to east across central Indiana on July 6th. Each afternoon, thunderstorms developed in the unstable airmass, gradually pushing south and east before dissipating quickly after loss of daytime heating. On July 6th, a broken line of strong-to-severe thunderstorms crossed the Ohio River from Indiana during the mid-afternoon hours. As the storms pushed across central Kentucky, downdraft CAPE of greater than 1200 J/kg helped damaging wind gusts reach the ground, and several wind damage reports were observed, mainly across north central Kentucky. On July 7th, lesser instability led to the development of garden-variety thunderstorms, with wind damage only being observed in a few of the strongest cells. Finally, on July 8th, clusters of strong and severe thunderstorms produced scattered wind damage across south central Kentucky, with flash flooding also being observed in Russell County due to repeated bursts of heavy rainfall.
episodes.171582: A weak low pressure system was located in central Missouri, with a slow moving warm front draped across southern Illinois. Widespread thunderstorms developed along the warm front during the pre-dawn hours, with the complex tracking southeast during the morning. The heaviest rains occurred near and south of I-72, where 2 to 4 inches of rain fell, resulting in a few instances of flash flooding.
episodes.171583: A weak low pressure system was located in southwestern Illinois on the afternoon of July 8, 2022, with a stationary front draped near the I-70 corridor. A secondary cold front pushed into central Illinois from the north, and scattered thunderstorms developed along both boundaries. As storm clusters progressed to the southeast, they produced isolated flash flooding, hail, and wind damage.
episodes.171676: A broken line of thunderstorms developed across southeast Georgia and moved into southeast South Carolina in the mid to late afternoon hours. One thunderstorm moved through Colleton County and produced isolated wind damage.
episodes.171680: A cluster of thunderstorms developed along the southeast Georgia coast in the early afternoon hours and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.171790: A short wave moved east along a stationary front that was along the I-70 corridor. Some of the storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.171791: A cold front moved through the region, triggering showers and storms. Some of the storms became severe producing damaging winds.
episodes.171792: A cold front moved through the region, triggering showers and storms. Some of the storms became severe producing damaging winds.
episodes.171980: An open wave moving up from the south initiated multiple hail producing storms, and at least one with estimated severe winds.
episodes.172009: A late season cold front pushed southward across Central Alabama on July 9th.  The air mass ahead of the front was very unstable with afternoon surface based CAPE of 4000-4500 J/kg and lifted indices around -7 Celsius.  PWAT's were above two inches which also supported heavy rainfall and flash flooding.
episodes.172036: A few isolated storms formed along a weak boundary in northern North Carolina, which resulted in a few downed trees in Yadkin and Wilkes counties.
episodes.172088: An open wave moving up from the south initiated multiple hail producing storms.
episodes.172090: Sufficient CAPE, SHEAR, dew points in the upper 50s, and southwest flow combined to produce severe weather.
episodes.172186: A cold front served as a focus for thunderstorm development across western into central Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 8th, with several reports of severe wind gusts received, including a wind gust over 80 mph recorded near Bessie, Oklahoma.
episodes.172293: Strong thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and produced gusty winds that caused damage in southwest Alabama.
episodes.172356: Surface high pressure to the southeast and a front approaching southeast Georgia resulted in southwesterly flow across the area. The east coast sea breeze was pinned along the I-95 corridor as the dominant west coast sea breeze shifted inland in the afternoon. Isolated strong storms developed along the sea breeze boundary collisions blowing shingles off a roof on Amelia Island. With a saturated airmass and slow storm motion, locally heavy rain of 2 to 3 inches fell and resulted in street flooding in Green Cove Springs.
episodes.172468: Rain showers produced heavy rain of 3 to 5 inches across the warned area. This led to flash flooding in Johnson county and Muscatine County.
episodes.172470: A line of scattered showers and thunderstorms moved southeastward across McDonough County. One of these storms produced a brief tornado that occurred in an open field near the Macomb Airport. There was no visible signs of damage to assign an EF-scale rating.
episodes.172494: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region.  There were a few reports of flooding and trees down across southwest Georgia.
episodes.172551: During the afternoon and evening, a few clusters of thunderstorms moved southeast across East Tennessee. Some isolated wind damage occurred with these clusters.
episodes.172553: A large complex of thunderstorms moved southeast from Kentucky and Middle Tennessee into East Tennessee in the late afternoon. Isolated wind damage occurred in a few areas.
episodes.172567: Afternoon thunderstorms formed across portions of the Texas Panhandle on the afternoon of the 8th due to instability and wind shear in the atmosphere. As a result, severe thunderstorms developed with reports of large hail and wind damage due to severe wind gusts.
episodes.172602: Strong diurnal heating resulted in ample instability, which allowed one severe thunderstorm to produce damaging winds in Yadkin County.
episodes.172604: A stalled frontal boundary to the north from the Mid-Mississippi Valley into the Ohio Valley and northern Virginia led to early morning storms north of the Carolinas. This led to numerous surface boundaries that aided thunderstorms to form along the Piedmont in the mid to late-afternoon hours. These storms tracked east-southeast in the evening to early overnight hours into the Sandhills and Coastal Plain. Many of the storms produced thunderstorm wind damage and a few also produced flash flooding.
episodes.172639: An area of 1 to 2 inches of rainfall occurred across the headwaters of the Little Sioux River on July 5 and resulted in a brief period of minor to locally moderate flooding.
episodes.172770: Some residual monsoonal moisture remained around the Rio Grande Valley of Texas with very weak flow aloft.  Slow moving storms developed over northeast El Paso which dropped 1 to 2 inches of rain quickly causing some localized flash flooding.
episodes.172810: Hot and sunny conditions aided formation of a dust devil which injured several people.
episodes.172861: Early morning convection produced numerous thunderstorms across the area. Given the early morning atmosphere there was not much wind damage reported with these storms, but a few isolated wind events occurred just south of Kansas City in Miami and Linn Counties. The worst of the damage was some power poles down near Parker, Kansas.
episodes.172864: On the overnight hours of July 7, into the morning hours of July 8, numerous thunderstorms moved through northern Missouri, producing scattered areas of wind damage.
episodes.172939: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over upstate South Carolina during the afternoon and moved southeast throughout the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced a microburst that caused significant damage in Anderson County.
episodes.172940: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed near the Blue Ridge escarpment during the afternoon and moved southeast throughout the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced locally damaging wind gusts in Rutherford County.
episodes.172984: Scattered thunderstorms once again affected Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours of July 8 into the early morning hours on July 9. Several reports of wind damage were received.
episodes.173067: Typical afternoon summertime showers and thunderstorms developed within a persistent and abnormally moist tropical airmass during the afternoon and evening of July 8th , aided by stout instability as a weak upper level disturbance moved around the eastern periphery of a retrograding upper level ridge. These storms produced numerous reports of trees and powerlines down and isolated flash flooding across portions of north Georgia and far east-central Georgia.
episodes.173627: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the Piedmont during the evening. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Union County.
